questions.question: For U(1) symmetry, what phenomenon occurs when two states are jointly processed, and how is it explained by the complementarity among members of the QFI family?

questions.answer_span: We show that, even for U (1) symmetry, a state with zero conversion rate to a given target can nevertheless increase the yield obtainable from another state when the two are processed jointly. In analogy with activation phenomena for channel capacities, we call this phenomenon asymmetry activation. This activation arises from complementarity among different members of the QFI family: distinct QFIs impose different constraints on the conversion rate, and jointly processing input states can enhance the rate beyond what either state alone can achieve.
